task.prompt:
Implement a PL/pgSQL procedure named sp. The procedure must accept exactly three parameters in this order: para_product_title of type text, para_product_id of type integer, and para_transaction_id of type integer. The procedure uses only the following tables and columns: Invoice_Line_Items.product_title, Invoice_Line_Items.product_id, and Invoice_Line_Items.invoice_number; Financial_Transactions.transaction_id, Financial_Transactions.transaction_amount, and Financial_Transactions.invoice_number. All comparisons use SQL equality semantics, so null is not considered equal to any value.

First, look at Invoice_Line_Items. If at least one row has product_title equal to para_product_title, update every row with that product_title by setting its product_id to the result of multiplying para_product_id by 2. Do not modify any other columns in those rows, and do not insert a new row in this case. If no row has product_title equal to para_product_title, insert a new row into Invoice_Line_Items with product_title set to para_product_title and product_id set to para_product_id. No other columns are explicitly assigned in the inserted row, so they receive whatever default or null values the database would normally apply. The update and insert are mutually exclusive: exactly one of them occurs.

Next, delete from Financial_Transactions every row whose transaction_id is strictly less than para_transaction_id. A row whose transaction_id equals para_transaction_id is not deleted. If para_transaction_id is null, no row satisfies this deletion.

Next, if para_transaction_id is strictly greater than 0, delete from Financial_Transactions every remaining row whose transaction_amount is strictly less than 0. Zero and positive transaction_amount values do not qualify. This deletion applies only to rows that remain after the previous transaction_id deletion. If para_transaction_id is 0, negative, or null, skip this amount-based deletion entirely.

Finally, after all earlier operations have completed, delete from Financial_Transactions every row whose invoice_number equals any non-null invoice_number currently present in Invoice_Line_Items in rows whose product_title equals para_product_title. This final deletion uses the Invoice_Line_Items rows as they exist after the earlier insert or update. A null invoice_number in Invoice_Line_Items does not match any Financial_Transactions.invoice_number. If no Invoice_Line_Items row has product_title equal to para_product_title at that point, no Financial_Transactions rows are deleted by this final step.

All steps must be performed in this exact order. The procedure does not contain explicit exception handling; if any operation raises an error, the procedure does not catch it and the error propagates to the caller.

Implement this as a PostgreSQL (PL/pgSQL) stored procedure named `sp` with the parameter list exactly `sp(para_product_title text, para_product_id integer, para_transaction_id integer)`. Return the complete stored procedure, and nothing else.
